note: The family 1 Duke William Mount (#106) was built for. The house holds nobody at all in the record — no census household has ever been filed there — so these eight are the first, and they come from a family account rather than a return. Horace and Sarah Kate are given what the account dates; the six children are created with names only, so that when a census page for the house turns up the entries attach to people already here instead of making second copies. No Thackeray was in the record before this.
source: A. Hagues, from the Fisher family account

people.bio: Horace Arthur Fisher, a lace industrialist, was the man 1 Duke William Mount was built for. Born in Hyson Green in 1854, he married Sarah Kate Thackeray in 1879 — the eldest daughter of John Thackeray, of another prominent Nottingham lace manufacturing family — and the couple moved into the house after the birth of their first child, James, in 1883. They had six children: James, Sybil, Horace (known as Frank), Geoffrey, John and Florence. The family's own business stood on Short Hill, and later in Radford.

occupations.notes: The family business, on Short Hill and later in Radford.
